source_text:
Εἰ γὰρ καὶ κατὰ σάρκα μέ τινες ἠθέλησαν πλανῆσαι, ἀλλὰ τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν. οἶδεν γάρ, πόθεν ἔρχεται καὶ ποῦ ὑπάγει, καὶ τὰ κρυπτὰ ἐλέγχει. ἐκραύγασα μεταξὺ ὤν, ἐλάλουν μεγάλῃ φωνῇ, θεοῦ φωνῇ: Τῷ ἐπισκοπῳ προσέχετε καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ καὶ διακόνοις.
οἱ δὲ ὑποπτεύσαντές με ὡς προειδότα τὸν μερισμόν τινων λέγειν ταῦτα: μάρτυς δέ μοι, ἐν ᾧ δέδεμαι, ὅτι ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης οὐκ ἔγνων. τὸ δὲ πνεῦμα ἐκήρυσσεν λέγον τάδε: Χωρὶς τοῦ ἐπισκόπου μηδὲν ποιεῖτε, τὴν σάρκα ὑμῶν ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ τηρεῖτε, τὴν ἕνωσιν ἀγαπᾶτε, τοὺς μερισμοὺς φεύγετε, μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ.
thought_title: The Spirit's cry for unity around the bishop
orientation: Ignatius is writing to the Philadelphians, recounting how he cried out with a divine voice among them, urging unity with the bishop, elders, and deacons.
pass_a_gloss: For even if some wanted to deceive me according to the flesh, yet the Spirit is not deceived, being from God. For it knows whence it comes and where it goes, and it exposes the hidden things. I cried out, being in the midst, I was speaking with a loud voice, with God's voice: 'Pay attention to the bishop and to the council of elders and to the deacons.' But some suspected me, as one who knew in advance the division of some, to say these things: but my witness, in whom I am bound, is that from human flesh I did not know. But the Spirit was proclaiming, saying these things: 'Without the bishop do nothing, keep your flesh as a temple of God, love the unity, flee the divisions, become imitators of Jesus Christ, as also he is of his Father.'

choices.term: τὸ πνεῦμα οὐ πλανᾶται ἀπὸ θεοῦ ὄν
choices.english: the Spirit is not deceived, being from God
choices.why: Keeps the causal participle 'being from God' as the reason the Spirit cannot be deceived, preserving the theological claim that the Spirit's divine origin guarantees its truthfulness.
rejected: the Spirit, since it is from God, is not led astray

choices.why: Renders the dative as instrumental, indicating the manner or source of the cry, matching Ignatius's claim that his shout was divinely inspired.
Uses the glossary term 'bishop' for ἐπίσκοπος and renders προσέχετε with its imperative force of heedful attention, preserving the command.

choices.term: τὴν σάρκα ὑμῶν ὡς ναὸν θεοῦ τηρεῖτε
choices.english: keep your flesh as a temple of God
choices.why: Uses the glossary term 'flesh' for σάρξ and keeps the simile 'as a temple of God' with the imperative 'keep', preserving the bodily and cultic imagery.
rejected: guard your body as God's temple

choices.term: μιμηταὶ γίνεσθε Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, ὡς καὶ αὐτὸς τοῦ πατρὸς αὐτοῦ
choices.english: become imitators of Jesus Christ, as also he is of his Father
choices.why: Keeps the elliptical second clause 'as also he is of his Father' to preserve the chain of imitation from believers through Christ to the Father.
rejected: be imitators of Jesus Christ, just as he imitates his Father

pass_b_english: Even if some people wanted to deceive me in the flesh, the Spirit is not deceived, because the Spirit is from God. For the Spirit knows where it comes from and where it is going, and it exposes hidden things. I cried out while I was among you. I spoke with a loud voice, with God's voice: "Pay attention to the bishop and to the council of elders and to the deacons."

Some of you suspected that I said these things because I knew in advance about the division of certain people. But the one in whom I am bound is my witness that I did not learn it from human flesh. The Spirit was proclaiming, saying these things: "Do nothing without the bishop. Keep your flesh as a temple of God. Love unity. Flee divisions. Become imitators of Jesus Christ, as also he is of his Father."

last_rejected.quote: I did not learn it from human flesh
last_rejected.why: ἔγνων means 'I knew', not 'I learned'. 'Learn' implies process; source denies human source of knowledge.
last_rejected.fix: I did not know it from human flesh
last_rejected.ruling: γινώσκω can mean 'learn' (BDAG 1b); 'did not learn from human flesh' fairly renders οὐκ ἔγνων ἀπὸ σαρκὸς ἀνθρωπίνης.
